[[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]] - [[:en:Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|Atago Shrine]] * [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]] - [[:en:Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|Atago Shrine]] * [[:en:Sannenzaka|Sannenzaka]] - Kyoto City, [[:en:Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto|Higashiyama Ward]] - [[:en:Kiyomizu-dera|Kiyomizu-dera]] == Important Monzen-machi and Toriimaemachi == * Cluster") * {{ill|Saga-Toriimoto|ja|嵯峨鳥居本|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga-Toriimoto|1=Saga Toriimoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11054653}} - [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Kyoto [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]] - [[:en:Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|Atago Shrine]] * [[:en:Sannenzaka|Sannenzaka]] - Kyoto City, [[:en:Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto|Higashiyama Ward]] - [[:en:Kiyomizu-dera|Kiyomizu-dera]] == Important Monzen-machi and Toriimaemachi == * [[:en:Sakamoto|Sakamoto (Ōtsu)]] - [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryaku-ji]] ("Monzen-machi and Satobō Cluster") * {{ill|Saga-Toriimoto|ja|嵯峨鳥居本|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga-Toriimoto|1=Saga Toriimoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11054653}} - [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Kyoto [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|[[:en:Sannenzaka|Sanneizaka]]]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent [[:en:Buddhist temple|Buddhist temples]] or [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrines]]. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher=[[:en:Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|World Encyclopedia]] 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as [[:en:Holy city|holy cities]] or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]], [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu City]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryakuji]] (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]], [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]], [[:en:Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto]] - [[:en:Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|Atago Shrine]] * [[:en:Sannenzaka|Sannenzaka]] - Kyoto City, [[:en:Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto|Higashiyama Ward]] - [[:en:Kiyomizu-dera|Kiyomizu-dera]] == Important Monzen-machi and Toriimaemachi == * [[:en:Sakamoto|Sakamoto (Ōtsu)]] - [[:en:Ōtsu|Ōtsu]], [[:en:Shiga Prefecture|Shiga Prefecture]] - [[:en:Hiyoshi Taisha|Hiyoshi Taisha]], [[:en:Enryaku-ji|Enryaku-ji]] ("Monzen-machi and Satobō Cluster") * {{ill|Saga-Toriimoto|ja|嵯峨鳥居本|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saga-Toriimoto|1=Saga Toriimoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11054653}} - [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Kyoto [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Sannenzaka|en|Sannenzaka|WD=Q11574990|lt=Sanneizaka}}]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|WD=Q5393308|lt=Buddhist temples}} or {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}}. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|en|Shiga Prefecture|WD=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ōtsu|en|Ōtsu|WD=Q202907|lt=Ōtsu City}} - {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|WD=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}}, {{ill|Enryaku-ji|en|Enryaku-ji|WD=Q917195|lt=Enryakuji}} (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Sannenzaka|en|Sannenzaka|WD=Q11574990|lt=Sanneizaka}}]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|WD=Q5393308|lt=Buddhist temples}} or {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}}. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|en|Shiga Prefecture|WD=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ōtsu|en|Ōtsu|WD=Q202907|lt=Ōtsu City}} - {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|WD=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}}, {{ill|Enryaku-ji|en|Enryaku-ji|WD=Q917195|lt=Enryakuji}} (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto Prefecture}}, {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto City}}, {{ill|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|en|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|WD=Q580186|lt=Ukyō-ku, Kyoto}} - {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|Atago Shrine Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|en|Shiga Prefecture|WD=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ōtsu|en|Ōtsu|WD=Q202907|lt=Ōtsu City}} - {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|WD=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}}, {{ill|Enryaku-ji|en|Enryaku-ji|WD=Q917195|lt=Enryakuji}} (categorized as "Monzen-machi and Sato-bo Group") * [[Sagatoriimoto]] - {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|en|Kyoto Prefecture|WD=Q120730|lt=Kyoto [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Sannenzaka|en|Sannenzaka|WD=Q11574990|lt=Sanneizaka|1=Sannenzaka}}]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|WD=Q5393308|lt=Buddhist temples|1=Buddhist temple}} or {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia|1=Heibonsha World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities|1=Holy city}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] - {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|en|Shiga Prefecture|WD=Q131358|lt=Shiga Prefecture|1=Shiga Prefecture}}, {{ill|Ōtsu|en|Ōtsu|WD=Q202907|lt=Ōtsu City|1=Ōtsu}} - {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Sannenzaka|en|Sannenzaka|WD=Q11574990|lt=Sanneizaka|1=Sannenzaka}}]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|WD=Q5393308|lt=Buddhist temples|1=Buddhist temple}} or {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia|1=Heibonsha World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities|1=Holy city}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[fa:شهر معبدی]][[ja:門前町]][[zh:門前町]] [[File:Sakamoto Otsu03s4592.jpg|thumb|Sakamoto]] [[File:Toriimoto03s3200.jpg|thumb|Sagatoriimoto]] [[File:Stone stairway Kiyomizu-dera.JPG|thumb|150px|{{ill|Sannenzaka|en|Sannenzaka|WD=Q11574990|lt=Sanneizaka|1=Sannenzaka}}]] '''Monzen-machi''' (門前町, monzen-machi) refers to a town formed around prominent {{ill|Buddhist temple|en|Buddhist temple|WD=Q5393308|lt=Buddhist temples|1=Buddhist temple}} or {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines|1=Shinto shrine}}. Specifically, for shrines, it is often called a '''Torii-mae Town''' (鳥居前町, torii-mae-machi). == Overview == Broadly speaking, settlements formed by followers of temples or shrines, including {{ill|Temples and Shrines|lt=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|ja|社家町|Shrines and Temples=Temples and Shrines|lt=Shrines and Temples|lt=shaji towns|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrines and Temples|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 社家}} and {{ill|Jinaimachi|ja|寺内町|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinaimachi|qq=}}, are also considered Monzen-machi. {{Cite web|和書|url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E9%96%80%E5%89%8D%E7%94%BA-143199#E4.B8.96.E7.95.8C.E5.A4.A7.E7.99.BE.E7.A7.91.E4.BA.8B.E5.85.B8.20.E7.AC.AC.EF.BC.92.E7.89.88|title=Monzen-machi|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|en|Heibonsha World Encyclopedia|WD=Q5698601|lt=World Encyclopedia|1=Heibonsha World Encyclopedia}} 2nd Edition / Kotobank|accessdate=2018-03-07}} Larger-scale examples may be defined as {{ill|Holy city|en|Holy city|WD=Q692581|lt=holy cities|1=Holy city}} or {{ill|Temple Precinct Cities|ja|境内都市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temple Precinct Cities|qq=}}. Historically, sites for urban formation included castles, ports, markets, and exchange hubs, with temples and shrines being among these. Monzen-machis form when shrine or temple workers and merchants serving pilgrims gather in front of large shrines or temples attracting many visitors. However, the establishment of monzen towns is not guaranteed by the scale of the religious institution, as certain temples historically prohibited public access.{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldtimes.co.jp/japan/20221119-166722/|title=70-Year-Old Thatch Roof Repair of Jionji Main Hall, a National Important Cultural Property in Yamagata Prefecture's Sagae City|publisher=The World Times|date=November 19, 2022|access-date=May 26, 2023}} Regions that still retain historical elements as monzen towns are designated as {{ill|Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|ja|重要伝統的建造物群保存地区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|1=Important Preservation Districts for Groups of Traditional Buildings|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q850649}}, with preservation measures enacted. Since 1998, the {{ill|National Monzen-machi Summit|ja|全国門前町サミット|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Monzen-machi Summit|1=National Monzen-machi Summit|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11389611}} has been held annually to promote exchanges between such towns. == Monzen-machis and Torii-mae Towns in Important Preservation Districts == * [[Sakamoto (Ōtsu City)|Sakamoto]]
